releases.body:
**17 changes since v1.0.4**

## Test

- **Fixed** Drop the PATH-wiping test that broke CI; trim comments `c8fd604`
  - Seven savepoint.test.ts tests failed on CI with an empty-error `git commit --allow-empty`. The cause was in a different file: the `sign --gen-key --backend minisign` test I added set
  - process.env.PATH = dir
  - to force minisign to be absent, and held it across an `await`. `bun test --parallel=2` runs two files in one process, so during that window any concurrent `execSync('git ...')` had no PATH and failed. savepoint.test.ts runs 35 savepoint.sh invocations, each spawning node 11 times — it is the file most likely to be mid-exec when the window opens.
  - Measured before assuming: savepoint.test.ts takes 57.8s at the base commit and 56.5s here, so nothing I changed made it slower. The suite growing was not the cause either; the PATH wipe was.
  - The test is removed rather than fixed. Forcing minisign absent needs a process-global mutation, and five lines of coverage do not justify a cross-file hazard. The pre-existing PATH writes in sign.test.ts and closure-runtime.test.ts are materially safer: they prepend rather than replace, or hold the value across synchronous calls with no yield point.
  - Comments trimmed across the files this branch touched: -169/+60. The reasoning that belongs in a commit message was sitting in the source.
- **Fixed** Ship trigger asserts Flow 9; revert cli help wording (coverage gate) `812c6c4`
  - heal cycle 1. Two findings from the Flow 4 audit:
  - test/cli.test.ts:1239 asserted the defect — it expected the ship row to read Flow 8. Updated the literal only; the assertion still pins the row count, the full "token — trigger — default — firing" shape and the ordering.
  - src/cli.ts is reverted to baseline. The two help strings said "wave" where the canon says flow stage, but touching the file pulls all 69KB of it into coverage-gate, which measures whole-file coverage: 1051/1323 lines = 79.44%, against a modified-file threshold of 90. Reaching that needs ~140 lines of new cli.ts coverage — a test mission, not a wording fix. Lowering the threshold or excluding the file is what the gate explicitly forbids, so the wording is deferred instead and recorded in the closure report. src/features.ts keeps its Flow 8 -> Flow 9 correction; it measures 97.20% and passes.

## Ci

- **Fixed** Release pre-flight runs the gate; workflows can no longer re-list it `9ae5ddf`
  - The manual release failed on `--check-sync is exclusive`. The guard was right, and what it exposed is worse than the error: that line read
  - validate-content.ts --check-manifest --check-docs --check-sync
  - and --check-sync process.exit(0)s as soon as it has an answer, so the two checks before it NEVER RAN. Every manual release has been pre-flighting plugin-copy sync and nothing else. The guard turned a silent skip into a loud failure on its first real caller, which is what it was written for.
  - Both release workflows now run `bun run gate` instead of hand-listing steps. release-manual ran 6 of the gate's 18 checks; release.yml ran 4. A tag could publish past checks the main branch is held to.
  - ci.yml already carries the rule: "One gate, one definition... CI used to re-list the steps by hand and the two drifted, omitting verify-install, gate-selftest, lane-base, verify-pack, build-hooks and --check-doc-integrity. Five capabilities shipped dead behind a green board." Prose did not hold it — this is the third failure of the same rule — so checkWorkflowGateDrift now fails any workflow that runs a script the gate already runs. gate-selftest is exempt: it is deliberately outside the gate.

## Readme

- **Docs** Fix unclear install-to-docs links, normalize install headings `34d625e`
  - README's Install section linked most platforms nowhere (Claude Code and
  - opencode blocks had no doc link at all; 7 platforms were grouped behind one
  - link to docs/install/index.md), and the Docs footer's Install line was
  - missing Cursor/Antigravity/Kimi/Pi even though those install docs exist.
  - - Add a direct per-platform doc link inside every <details> block.
  - - Add the 4 missing platforms to the footer's Install line.
  - - Normalize docs/install/claude.md and opencode.md to the same
  - Install / Verify-update-remove / Clean-uninstall heading shape the other
  - 8 install docs already use.
  - - Drop README's "Try it in 60 seconds" section: word-for-word duplicate of
  - "Quick start" above it: freed the word budget the link fixes needed.
  - Verified: typecheck, full test suite (1081 pass), validate-content
  - (--check-writing/--check-doc-integrity/--check-docs), check-doc-links —
  - all green.

## Dispatch

- **Fixed** Stop luffy-orchestrator from running as an isolated subagent `75a5e16`
  - Claude Code (and likely Copilot) auto-register every content/agents/*.md
  - file as a Task/Agent-tool subagent_type, identical to worker personas
  - (Zoro, Brook, Robin, Jinbe). luffy-orchestrator's own persona doc already
  - said "Embodied by the main thread ... never dispatches another crew
  - member", but nothing enforced it: a bare @-mention or agent invocation
  - spun up the captain as a fresh, zero-context background instance that
  - skipped Flow 0 triage/planning and ran the whole mission hidden from the
  - user until it returned.
  - - luffy-orchestrator.md: add a dispatch guard that refuses to execute when
  - invoked with no inherited mission context, and redirects the caller to
  - /mugiwara inline instead.
  - - harness-matrix.md: name the real difference between opencode's
  - foreground persona-switch and Claude Code/Copilot's background isolated
  - dispatch; list the 4 dispatch-worthy personas vs the 10 inline-only ones;
  - flag Copilot as unverified rather than assumed-safe.
  - - README.md, install/claude.md: one-line entry-point correction each.
  - - validate-content.ts + validate-content.test.ts: new doc-integrity rule
  - (with a red/green proof) so the guard can't silently regress.
  - No metadata.agents/manifest schema change — every install still ships the
  - whole crew (AGENTS.md invariant), this is guard text + docs + a validator
  - rule. Verified: typecheck, full test suite (1081 pass), validate-content
  - (manifest/docs/doc-integrity/writing), check-doc-links, verify-install,
  - and 12/12-platform conformance all green.

## Docs

- State the /mugiwara entry point where people actually look first `696d896`
  - Both entry points (natural language, /mugiwara <request>) and the
  - never-a-subagent-picker warning were only spelled out in
  - docs/install/claude.md. README's Quick Start and docs/getting-started.md
  - (the canonical "how do I start" page) didn't mention /mugiwara as an
  - equally valid way to open a mission.
  - - docs/getting-started.md: "Start a mission" now names both entry points
  - and restates which 4 personas are the only ones designed to run isolated.
  - - README.md: Quick Start's ask line now names /mugiwara alongside chat.
  - Verified: typecheck, full test suite (1081 pass), validate-content
  - (--check-writing/--check-doc-integrity/--check-docs), check-doc-links —
  - all green.

## Test

- **Fixed** Engage before writing artifacts in E3 guard fixtures — marker anchor made reversed order flaky `d6cb581`
  - The E3 guard fixtures wrote the artifact before engaging, so the artifact's
  - mtime was older than the marker's first_seen by the marker hook's spawn time.
  - artifactWorkNow() only counts mtimes within 1s of the anchor, and spawn cost
  - runs 0.3-0.7s idle / past 1.7s under the 8-worker gate, so the fixture was a
  - coin flip: 10/12 counted with the old order, 12/12 with engage first.
  - The guard is correct here — an artifact written before mugiwara was engaged is
  - out of scope for a mugiwara-session check, and the anchor is stamped when the
  - marker hook runs, so spawn latency is upstream of the anchor and cannot widen
  - the real-flow gap. Fixing the fixture, not the tolerance.
